chapter: Night life, Guy Kelly and Chicago youth
title: Drinking on the job, walking the bars, Monday jail
summary: Musicians were allowed to drink on the job and walked uptown bar to bar, and he recalls being jailed after a shooting.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: You say you had a lot of problems, do you think you had a lot of problems with the musician getting him drunk like that on the job? No, they didn't get drunk on the job, you see. They were allowed to drink on the job.
Yeah, they didn't get drunk on the job. And stuff like stuff like stuff stuff

The job is when they get off from work, some of them wouldn't go home until the time to come back to work the next night and all that kind of stuff. Nobody never walked or rode home. See they used to have dance halls up and down, and they'd all meet at the E-light on Ramport Street in the morning. You know what I'm saying? And they'd walk up all the barrooms, all the way uptown, you know, for Andrew Anderson, he was one of them. Yeah. Or Foster's cousin.
And they would walk, they would never ride uptown.
No, you see, because we'd walk, you see, because we'd go in them places and everybody knew them, they had credit accounts and bad liquor, you know, that spook down.
You could throw all the bars before you get home? Huh?

Might take a whole day to get home, you could throw all those bars. You could throw all these, you could throw them in there. And they went ahead and join that, you understand? And then we went back down to the entertainers downtown there, where Russ had, he used to put us in jail every Monday. Every Monday? Every Monday. And get right out. Why did he do that? Why did they put you in jail? I don't know. We just picked us up, raved the place. How long did you stay in jail? Until they called our name and we come right out. I see we was up there in Carlton playing one night, with Handy's job, with Law & Quarter. And all we were playing down handy, we got half loaded and was playing down and we started shooting in the hand and got shot in the foot or something like that. And they put us all in jail. And we went up there and brought them to the hospital and said, where was you when the shooting started? And I said, I don't want to play in jail. Well there used to be another guy who used to play up a lot of trumpets. He'd come down there with Handy and what's he called, he used to play all that trumpet like Lewis Armstrong.
